author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Hasbro’s move from Pawtucket to Boston now has a specific deadline for hundreds of Rhode Island positions. An Oct. 8 Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification, or WARN, filing says 587 employees at the toy and game company’s Rhode Island operations are affected by the planned closure of the Pawtucket site on Dec. 24. Employees who accept and complete a transfer to Hasbro’s new Boston headquarters are expected to continue working, while positions held by workers who do not make the move are set to end on that date, according to the filing and [Providence Business News](https://pbn.com/hasbro-offers-587-pawtucket-workers-jobs-at-boston-headquarters/?amp=1).

That distinction matters: the notice does not establish that Hasbro will immediately eliminate all 587 jobs. It identifies the positions covered by the Rhode Island closure and gives the company a legal timetable for the transition. Hasbro had not confirmed how many employees planned to accept the Boston offer when [WBUR reported](https://www.wbur.org/news/2026/10/14/boston-hasbro-relocation-pawtucket-workers) on the filing. The number who ultimately relocate, leave the company or find another arrangement remains unknown.

Workers who transfer are expected to begin at 400 Summer Street in Boston’s Seaport District on Jan. 4, 2027, according to [Boston.com’s report](https://www.boston.com/news/business/2026/10/14/hasbro-tells-rhode-island-workers-move-to-boston-or-lose-your-job/). That creates a short gap between the last scheduled day at the Pawtucket operation and the planned start in Boston, although the company’s notice says employees who accept and complete the transfer are not expected to experience an interruption in employment. The notice itself does not say how many workers will accept the offer.

Rhode Island’s Department of Labor and Training describes WARN as a federal notice process for covered plant closings and mass layoffs. The agency says employers with at least 100 full-time workers may have to give 60 days’ advance notice when they close a facility or discontinue an operating unit, and that notices should identify the work site, effective dates and number of affected workers. The department’s [WARN page](https://dlt.ri.gov/employers/worker-adjustment-and-retraining-notification-warn) listed the notices as updated Oct. 13.

The filing gives the company’s long-planned relocation a more concrete workforce impact than its earlier public timeline. Hasbro announced in September 2025 that it would move its Rhode Island operations to a new Boston headquarters and said at least 700 full-time employees were expected to transition by the end of 2026. The company described the new facility as seven floors and 265,000 square feet at 400 Summer Street. That [announcement](https://newsroom.hasbro.com/node/36016/pdf) also said the Boston office would house the principal headquarters for the toy, game and licensing businesses and most corporate services.

Hasbro’s latest annual filing separately said the company expected to move from its Pawtucket offices during the fourth quarter of 2026 and later list the Pawtucket properties for sale. The filing described the Pawtucket headquarters as approximately 343,000 square feet, with an adjacent building of about 23,000 square feet. Those properties and the employees who work there are the local side of a corporate decision that will shift headquarters functions across the state line. [Hasbro’s 2025 annual report](https://newsroom.hasbro.com/static-files/9c424664-f3c7-4b89-baa4-21b7b2755082) provides the company’s earlier real-estate and relocation description.

The consequences extend beyond the workers’ commutes. Pawtucket Mayor Don Grebien told WBUR that the company should meet with city officials about the transition, the effect on employees and the future of the property. Bryant University economics lecturer Liam Rice told the station that losing hundreds of jobs can reduce spending at nearby restaurants, bars and other businesses. Those comments describe potential local effects, not a measured forecast of how much spending Pawtucket will lose.

The state is preparing for workers who decide the Boston commute is not workable. The director of Rhode Island’s Department of Labor and Training told WBUR that the agency plans to hold a major job fair next month to help Hasbro employees find other opportunities. The company’s public record still leaves several questions open, including how many of the 587 workers will transfer, what will happen to the Pawtucket properties and whether the Boston office will reach the earlier target of at least 700 transitioning employees. The next fixed dates are Dec. 24 in Pawtucket and Jan. 4 in Boston.
dek: A new WARN filing says 587 Pawtucket positions are affected by the Dec. 24 closure date, with employees offered continued work after transferring to Boston.
headline: Hasbro relocation puts 587 Pawtucket positions on Dec. 24 deadline
sourceName: Hasbro WARN notice filed with Rhode Island Department of Labor and Training
seoTitle: Hasbro relocation puts 587 Pawtucket positions on deadline
seoDescription: A WARN filing says 587 Hasbro positions in Pawtucket are affected by the Dec. 24 closure date as the company moves headquarters to Boston.
